Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS and FSR: The statement remains cautiously optimistic—activity and employment continue to firm, policy is still highly accommodative even as asset purchases begin to taper, and the Committee stands ready to adjust if inflation persists. The FSR adds caution via elevated valuations, compressed risk premiums, vulnerabilities in nonbank funding markets, and high business leverage. However, the latest SLOOS tilts the outlook modestly more positive for credit supply and demand: banks broadly eased lending standards across residential real estate, HELOCs, consumer (including credit cards and autos), multifamily and nonfarm nonresidential CRE; many banks increased credit card limits and reduced auto loan rates; and demand was reported stronger for consumer loans with expectations of stronger demand for C&I and credit cards. Foreign banks also eased CRE standards with stronger CRE loan demand. Offsetting this, some institutions reported weaker current demand in C&I and autos, and a few categories saw unchanged standards or demand. Net effect: credit availability and expected demand are improving, supporting the flow of credit the FOMC highlights, but vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR keep the tone guarded. Accordingly, sentiment is revised modestly higher but still only slightly positive.
